newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Egypt lifts ban on live Irish cattle imports.
newsitem.headline: Egypt lifts ban on live Irish cattle imports.

text.p: Ireland's agriculture ministry said on Friday that Egypt had agreed to resume imports of live Irish cattle.
Egypt banned imports of Irish cattle ready for slaughter in January because of a rise in the incidence of bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) or so-called "mad cow disease" in the Irish herd.
"Egypt is a highly significant market for live cattle, worth over 120 million Irish pounds ($177 million) per annum," Irish agriculture minister Ivan Yates said.
"The decision to re-open the market will give a major boost to the Irish cattle and beef sector in the period ahead, especially in regard to the seasonal autumn supplies."

The president of the Irish Farmers' Association, John Donnelly, also welcomed the announcement and said he hoped it would ease the way for diplomatic efforts to reopen Ireland's cattle trade with Libya.
The Egyptian decision to lift the ban was widely expected after intensive diplomatic efforts by the Irish authorities.
